1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands (unread inbox for your task, your session's runtime/tokens, other live
34	runs) — read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone.
35	
36	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
37	
38	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
39	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
40	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
41	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
42	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
43	
44	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
45	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
46	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
47	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
48	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
49	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
50	
51	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
52	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
53	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
54	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
55	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
56	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
57	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
58	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
59	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
60	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
61	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
62	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
63	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
64	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
65	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
66	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
67	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
68	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
69	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
70	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
71	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
72	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
73	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
74	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
75	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
76	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
77	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
78	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
79	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
80	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
81	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
82	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
83	
84	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
85	
86	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
87	
88	| Variable | Meaning |
89	|---|---|
90	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
91	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
92	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
93	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
94	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
95	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
96	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
97	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
98	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
99	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
100	
101	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
102	
103	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
104	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
105	
106	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
107	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
108	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
109	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
110	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
111	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
112	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
113	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
114	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
115	
116	## One-shot discipline (important)
117	
118	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
119	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
120	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
121	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
122	
123	## Pick the highest-value work
124	
125	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
126	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
127	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
128	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
129	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
130	
131	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
132	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
133	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
134	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
135	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
136	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
137	(it returns to the queue).
138	
139	## Fresh-context checkpoints
140	
141	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
142	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
143	checkpoints:
144	
145	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
146	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
147	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
148	  clean/build result.
149	
150	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
151	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
152	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
153	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
154	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
155	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
156	terminal `done` claim.
157	
158	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
159	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
160	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
161	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
162	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
163	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
164	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
165	
166	## Warnings are work
167	
168	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
169	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
170	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
171	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
172	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
173	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
174	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
175	why.
176	
177	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
178	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
179	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
180	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
181	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
182	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
183	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
184	
185	## Do the work (Lean)
186	
187	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
188	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
189	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
190	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
191	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
192	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
193	configured final build covers the same files.
194	
195	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
196	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
197	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
198	mathlib — query it:
199	
200	| You want | Use | Not |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
203	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
204	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
205	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
206	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
207	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
208	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
209	
210	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
211	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
212	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
213	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
214	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
215	back to grep.
216	
217	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
218	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
219	
220	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
221	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
222	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
223	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
224	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
225	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
226	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
227	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
228	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
229	
230	## Read the other projects
231	
232	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
233	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
234	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
235	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
236	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
237	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
238	
239	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
240	
241	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
242	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
243	needs no permission.
244	
245	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
246	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
247	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
248	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
249	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
250	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
251	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
252	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
253	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
254	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
255	
256	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
257	
258	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
259	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
260	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
261	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
262	
263	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
264	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
265	
266	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
267	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
268	  as **memory**.
269	
270	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
271	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
272	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
273	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
274	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
275	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
276	shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
277	
278	## Resuming after an interruption
279	
280	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
281	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
282	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
283	
284	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
285	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
286	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
287	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
288	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
289	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
290	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
291	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
292	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
293	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
294	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
295	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
296	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
297	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
298	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
299	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
300	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
301	
302	## Final report (your last message)
303	
304	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
305	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
306	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
307	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
308	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
309	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
310	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
311	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
312	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
313	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
314	not by itself a reason to stop.
315	
316	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
317	
318	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
319	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
320	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
321	`subagents` skill):
322	
323	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
324	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
325	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
326	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
327	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
328	
329	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-inbox

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience).
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- Kinds: `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). A long unstructured blob is hard to scan.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what you did; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the comment body; the author is set automatically. Drop a comment at each **key advance**
  while you work an item (a milestone reached, a route ruled out, a blocker hit),

"""Advisory health checks for the human/agent-maintained work queues.

These checks deliberately never mutate state or fail a command.  They make the
workspace-hygiene guidance executable and visible to every CLI caller while
leaving room for a human or agent to decide that an unusually large collection
is intentional.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from .clock import utc_now
from .inbox import InboxItem, InboxKind, InboxStatus
from .roadmap import RoadmapItem, RoadmapStatus
from .tasks import HorizonTask, TaskStatus


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AdvisoryHealthLimits:
    """Central defaults for CLI collection-health warnings."""

    open_memories: int = 10
    open_info: int = 4
    open_inbox: int = 30
    open_tasks: int = 12
    active_roadmap: int = 8
    stale_running_task_hours: int = 24


DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS = AdvisoryHealthLimits()


def _as_utc(value: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Normalize legacy naive timestamps before comparing their age."""
    if value.tzinfo is None:
        return value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return value.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def inbox_health_warnings(
    items: Sequence[InboxItem], limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings for an inbox whose open working set may need pruning."""
    open_items = [item for item in items if item.status is InboxStatus.OPEN]
    warnings: list[str] = []
    counts = {
        kind: sum(item.kind is kind for item in open_items)
        for kind in (InboxKind.MEMORY, InboxKind.INFO)
    }
    if counts[InboxKind.MEMORY] > limits.open_memories:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {counts[InboxKind.MEMORY]} open memory items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_memories}) — archive stale, "
            "superseded, or no-longer-key memories if this is not intentional."
        )
    if counts[InboxKind.INFO] > limits.open_info:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {counts[InboxKind.INFO]} open info items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_info}) — archive notices that "
            "have been consumed if this is not intentional."
        )
    working_set = [item for item in open_items if item.kind is not InboxKind.PROTECTION]
    if len(working_set) > limits.open_inbox:
        warnings.append(
            f"Inbox has {len(working_set)} open non-protection items "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_inbox}) — review duplicates and "
            "stale items; use `inbox complete` or `inbox archive` where appropriate."
        )
    return warnings


def task_health_warnings(
    tasks: Sequence[HorizonTask],
    limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS,
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings for an oversized task queue or apparently orphaned runs."""
    open_statuses = {TaskStatus.QUEUED, TaskStatus.RUNNING, TaskStatus.BLOCKED}
    open_tasks = [task for task in tasks if task.status in open_statuses]
    warnings: list[str] = []
    if len(open_tasks) > limits.open_tasks:
        warnings.append(
            f"Task queue has {len(open_tasks)} open tasks "
            f"(recommended maximum {limits.open_tasks}) — review whether some "
            "objectives are done, blocked, cancelled, duplicated, or better kept "
            "only as roadmap milestones."
        )

    cutoff = _as_utc(now or utc_now()) - timedelta(hours=limits.stale_running_task_hours)
    stale = [
        task for task in tasks
        if task.status is TaskStatus.RUNNING and _as_utc(task.updated_at) < cutoff
    ]
    if stale:
        shown = ", ".join(task.id for task in stale[:4])
        more = f" (+{len(stale) - 4} more)" if len(stale) > 4 else ""
        warnings.append(
            f"Task(s) {shown}{more} have remained running for more than "
            f"{limits.stale_running_task_hours}h — confirm a run is still live or "
            "reset their status if it ended unexpectedly."
        )
    return warnings


def roadmap_health_warnings(
    items: Sequence[RoadmapItem], limits: AdvisoryHealthLimits = DEFAULT_HEALTH_LIMITS
) -> list[str]:
    """Warnings when too many roadmap milestones claim simultaneous focus."""
    active = [item for item in items if item.status is RoadmapStatus.ACTIVE]
    if len(active) <= limits.active_roadmap:
        return []
    return [
        f"Roadmap has {len(active)} active items "
        f"(recommended maximum {limits.active_roadmap}) — consider marking "
        "deferred work pending, or leave the broader focus active intentionally."
    ]

But note the arithmetic before planning the packet route: A.colength j = Gamma(pieces j) / span {A.eqn j}, and A.eqn j is a NONZERODIVISOR (derived, DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular; primitive field LocalEquations.regular, DivisorClass.lean:120).
